original_title: Modular PEGylation Confers Reduced Immune-Cell Uptake and Enhanced Pharmacokinetic Performance to Encapsulin Protein Nanocages
title: PEGylating encapsulin nanocages so macrophages stop noticing them
blurb: SpyTag/SpyCatcher chemistry pins PEG onto the surface of an Am-S encapsulin nanocage site-specifically, hitting 82% conjugation efficiency and roughly 49 PEG chains per 60-subunit cage. That cuts macrophage uptake and stretches circulation time, going after the immune clearance problem that's actually been holding these back as delivery vehicles.

original_title: Well-Defined Molecular Alkali Metal Catalysts for Mild and Selective Reduction of Carboxylic Acids by Hydrosilylation
title: Carboxylic acids to alcohols, catalyzed by something cheaper than a transition metal
blurb: Hydrosilylative reduction of carboxylic acids usually means a transition metal wrestling with poor selectivity, narrow functional-group tolerance, and heat. This swaps in well-defined alkali metal catalysts instead, cheap and easy to make, for mild, selective reduction straight to the alcohol.

original_title: From Bench to Bedside: A Critical Appraisal of Somatostatin Receptor Antagonists in the Theranostic Management of Neuroendocrine Neoplasms
title: Somatostatin receptor antagonists, from bench toward the clinic
blurb: A critical appraisal of where somatostatin receptor antagonists actually stand for theranostic use in neuroendocrine neoplasms. Review only, no new data, just a stock-take of how close the antagonist approach is to catching up with the agonist tracers already in clinical use.

original_title: Electronic Communication Between Ferroelectric Surface Dipoles and Catalytic Active Sites Under Diverse Reaction Conditions
title: Can a ferroelectric flip talk to the metal sitting on top of it
blurb: Static catalyst design has a ceiling, so this checks whether flipping a ferroelectric support's surface dipole can electronically communicate with supported transition-metal active sites across a range of reaction conditions. If that coupling holds up broadly, it's a path to catalysts tuned electronically on the fly instead of redesigned from scratch each time.

original_title: High-toughness chitosan-based films fabricated by crosslinking via Mannich multicomponent reaction for strawberry preservation.
title: Mannich chemistry toughens up chitosan film for strawberry packaging
blurb: Crosslinking chitosan through a Mannich multicomponent reaction produces high-toughness films, tested here for strawberry preservation. More a packaging paper than a chemistry one, but the toughness gain is the actual point.

original_title: Proximity Labeling-Assisted Flow Cytometry Improves Fluorescence Contrast in Extracellular Vesicle-Enriched Fractions
title: Tagging targets near CHL1 so flow cytometry can actually see the EVs
blurb: Extracellular vesicles are too small and the disease-relevant ones too scarce for standard flow cytometry to pick out. This workflow runs serum EV fractions through size-exclusion chromatography, then uses CHL1-antibody-triggered EMARS labeling to deposit fluorescein on everything nearby, boosting the signal enough for ordinary flow cytometers to read it.

original_title: Mechanism and Origins of Enantioselectivity of Rhodium‐Catalyzed [4+3] Annulation of Benzosilacyclobutenes with 7‐Oxabenzonorbornadienes
title: Why the obvious mechanism for this Rh-catalyzed [4+3] doesn't work
blurb: DFT on the Rh-catalyzed annulation of benzosilacyclobutenes with oxabenzonorbornadienes: C-Si oxidative addition happens fine, but the expected migratory insertion followed by β-O elimination is kinetically infeasible. Computations trace an alternative route that also accounts for the enantioselectivity. Purely computational, so it's an explanation for an existing reaction, not a new one.

original_title: Cofixation of NH3 and CO2 through Cyclic Diarylchloronium Salt-Triggered Ring-Opening Bifunctionalization of Unstrained Cyclic Amines
title: Fixing NH3 and CO2 together by cracking open a cyclic amine
blurb: A diarylchloronium salt opens up unstrained cyclic amines and stitches in both aqueous NH3 and CO2 in one step, giving carbamates with a free amino group in high yield and with regiospecificity. It still works with dilute CO2, so this is aimed at waste gas streams, not just pure cylinders.

original_title: Forging ammonia with iron and light from water and nitrogen
title: Fixing nitrogen with iron, light, and water instead of Haber-Bosch
blurb: Iron salts paired with a molybdenum catalyst drive light-powered reduction of atmospheric N2 to ammonia, using water itself as the electron donor rather than a sacrificial reagent. Billed as a new pathway for one of chemistry's most energy-hungry reactions, but this is photochemistry on paper, not a Haber-Bosch replacement yet.

original_title: From Bench to Bedside: A Critical Appraisal of Somatostatin Receptor Antagonists in the Theranostic Management of Neuroendocrine Neoplasms.
title: Grading somatostatin receptor antagonists for neuroendocrine tumor theranostics
blurb: A bench-to-bedside review sizing up antagonist tracers against the established agonist-based approach for imaging and treating neuroendocrine neoplasms. No new data here, just the appraisal, so it's a stock-take rather than a result.

original_title: Theranostic Radiopharmaceutical-Guided Robotic Surgery for Precision Tumor Resection and Targeted Elimination of Residual Disease in Digestive System Malignancies
title: Ga-68/Lu-177 FAPI bracketing robotic surgery to mop up leftover GI tumor
blurb: A prospective feasibility study in 36 patients with colorectal, gastric, and pancreatic cancer: FAP-targeted Ga-68 FAPI-46 PET/CT maps disease before surgery, robotic resection is guided by the tracer signal in real time, then Lu-177 FAPI-46 goes after whatever residual disease is left. It's a feasibility study, so it shows the workflow can run, not yet that it cuts recurrence.

original_title: Skeletal Distortion Manipulation in 2D–3D-Fused Boron Clusters Enables Solid-State Luminescence and Photothermal Conversion
title: 3D boron clusters that glow through distortion, not rigidity
blurb: Two boron cluster-fused heterocycles, one with phosphorus and one with nitrogen, show aggregation-induced emission in the solid state, but through skeletal distortion rather than the usual restricted-intramolecular-motion story. The same scaffolds also do photothermal conversion, so one 3D platform covers both light output and heat generation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Decagram-Scale Synthesis of GB13 and Remodeling to the Galbulimima Alkaloids
title: One scalable route into GB13, then branching into the rest of the Galbulimima alkaloids
blurb: The Galbulimima alkaloids hit muscarinic and opioid receptors and, by tradition, reach the brain when the plant extract is ingested, but each scaffold has needed its own from-scratch synthesis. This paper makes GB13 at decagram scale and remodels that one intermediate into the rest of the family, which is what actually lets people study alkaloids that were previously too scarce to get hold of.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: A Library of Iron and α-Ketoglutarate Dependent Dioxygenases Enables the Synthesis of Six Fungal Natural Products
title: A dioxygenase library for hydroxylating fungal natural products where you want
blurb: Site-selective C-H hydroxylation is usually the bottleneck in these syntheses, and matching one biosynthetic enzyme to one target rarely works out. Here a library of iron/alpha-ketoglutarate dioxygenases stands in as a screenable toolkit instead, and it's enough to build six different fungal natural products.

original_title: Integrating complementary biological information for multi-objective enzyme engineering
title: Teaching a ketoreductase to be good at three things at once
blurb: A machine learning framework combines sparse experimental measurements with evolutionary and structural data to engineer the ketoreductase Gre2, and gets simultaneous gains in catalytic performance, protein yield, and thermal stability instead of trading one for the others. That trade-off is normally the whole problem with industrial biocatalyst engineering, so avoiding it is the actual result here.

original_title: Oxidation-Enabled Assembly Forms a Diatomic Catalyst for Propane Dehydrogenation
title: A whiff of CO2 keeps the propane dehydrogenation catalyst from clumping
blurb: These dual-atom catalysts usually sinter apart under the reducing conditions propane dehydrogenation needs. Here cofeeding trace CO2 or H2O oxidizes In into In3+ anchored on silica defects and Rh into Rh3+ linked by framework oxygen, and the two assemble into a Rh-In diatomic site instead of aggregating. Fighting a reduction problem by adding an oxidant is the counterintuitive part.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Precise pH-triggered cleavage of PEG-lipid conjugates drives endosomal escape of siRNA from fusogenic lipid-based nanoparticles.
title: A PEG coat on the LNP that unclips itself once it's inside the endosome
blurb: PEG-lipid conjugates on these fusogenic siRNA nanoparticles are built to cleave at endosomal pH, shedding the PEG right when the particle needs to fuse and let the siRNA out. Standard PEG dilemma, solved with a pH switch instead of just picking a density and living with the tradeoff.

original_title: Diastereo- and Enantioselective Photobiocatalytic α-Alkylation of α-Heteroaryl Amines Enabled by Pyridoxal Photochemistry
title: Evolving an enzyme to do radical chemistry PLP was never built for
blurb: Directed evolution of thermophilic threonine aldolases, screened through high-throughput photobiocatalysis, turned up PLP-dependent enzymes that mediate radical C-C bond formation on α-heteroaryl amines, a substrate class barely touched before. The payoff is diastereo- and enantioselective access to chiral aliphatic amines carrying pyridines and other N-heterocycles, not just a proof-of-concept substrate.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Electrochemical Synthesis of Macrocyclic Iminoisocoumarins by Rh-Catalyzed Intramolecular Vinylic C–H Activation/Heterocyclization
title: Electrochemistry stands in for the oxidant in a Rh-catalyzed macrocyclization
blurb: Rh(III)-catalyzed vinylic C-H activation and heterocyclization run under electrooxidation instead of a stoichiometric chemical oxidant, building iminoisocoumarin-braced macrocycles from 13 to 28 members in good yield with tight regioselectivity. They isolated the Rh(I) sandwich intermediate and backed it with cyclic voltammetry, so the proposed Rh(III/I) cycle isn't just hand-waving.

original_title: Room-Temperature Adsorption on Magnetite Induces Spontaneous Fragmentation of Early Transition-Metal Size-Selected Nanoclusters
title: Just landing on magnetite is enough to shatter these nanoclusters
blurb: Size-selected W, Mo, and Ta clusters soft-landed on reconstructed Fe3O4(001) fragment spontaneously at room temperature, no reaction turnover required, just adsorption. Not great if the plan was to lean on strong metal-support interaction to keep a nanocluster catalyst in one piece under real operating conditions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Non-Destructive Chemoselective Labeling and Bioorthogonal Enrichment of Pseudouridine-Containing RNA via Facile N 1-Selective Functionalization
title: Tagging pseudouridine without torching it first
blurb: A phosphate-promoted reaction lets α-methylene-γ-butyrolactone derivatives functionalize pseudouridine's N1 position selectively in water, giving a mild, nondestructive handle for bioorthogonal enrichment. Ψ is the most abundant RNA modification, and up to now mapping it has mostly meant harsh chemistry, so a gentle tag is the actual news.

original_title: AstraZeneca to hire 800+ for ADC cancer drug facility in Singapore - Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB)
title: AstraZeneca is staffing up an ADC plant in Singapore, 800-plus jobs
blurb: AstraZeneca is hiring more than 800 people for a new antibody-drug conjugate manufacturing facility in Singapore, per the Singapore EDB. Another data point that ADC manufacturing capacity, not the chemistry, is the thing everyone's racing to build out.

original_title: Active Confinement Catalysis Powered by Mechanical Force.
title: Powering a catalytic pocket with mechanical force instead of letting substrates wander in
blurb: Enzyme mimics usually rely on a static pocket and passive diffusion to find substrates, which caps the rate and demands a good size and electronic match. Borrowing the trick biological ion pumps use to move ions uphill, this is a solid-state mechanochemical setup where mechanical input actively drives a confinement and pumping cycle out of equilibrium, rather than waiting on stochastic collisions.

original_title: Beyond Symmetric Motifs: Asymmetric Small-Molecule Recognition Directs a New Poly(adenine) Assembly
title: A lopsided little molecule that reprograms poly(adenine) into something new
blurb: Only two small molecules were known to template these DNA hybrid assemblies before, and both worked through symmetric hydrogen-bonding faces. 3-methylxanthine has mismatched faces instead and still directs poly(deoxyadenylic) acid into a new cooperative arrangement, confirmed through preorganization tests, face modification, and nucleobase engineering. Breaks the assumption that the small molecule has to be symmetric.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: An in vivo chemical genetic approach for targeted glycoproteome analysis in Drosophila melanogaster
title: Giving fruit flies the machinery to tag their own glycoproteome
blurb: FlyMOE is a transgenic Drosophila platform that biosynthetically installs bioorthogonally-tagged monosaccharides straight into the glycoproteome, so glycoprotein profiling happens in vivo instead of the usual in vitro workaround. Fly genetics lets you dial in developmental stage, driver line, and even which glycosyltransferase is active, which is a real handle on where and when glycosylation happens rather than just that it does.

original_title: Reconstruction of a 30,000-Year-Old Biosynthetic Gene Cluster Reveals Lasso Peptides Formed by a Highly Tolerant Cyclase
title: A 30,000-year-old gene cluster still knows how to make a lasso peptide
blurb: Mining metagenomes from prehistoric dental calculus turned up a distinct lasso peptide cyclase lineage tied to oral Actinomyces, running back through the Paleolithic. They reconstructed a roughly 30,000-year-old biosynthetic gene cluster from that lineage, expressed it, and got a cyclase that's unusually tolerant of substrate variation. A new pocket of lasso peptide diversity that's been sitting in fossilized plaque the whole time.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Purification and surface functionalization of Cyclotella meneghiniana frustules as supports for immobilizing xylose isomerase.
title: Diatom shells repurposed as scaffolding for xylose isomerase
blurb: Purified frustules from the diatom Cyclotella meneghiniana, surface-functionalized and used as a solid support for immobilizing xylose isomerase. Silica the diatom already built for you instead of a synthetic carrier.

original_title: Mechanochemical Access to 2,4-Diaroyl-5-aminothiazoles from β-Ketothioamides at Room Temperature
title: Thiazoles from a mortar and pestle, ten minutes, no metal
blurb: Grinding β-ketothioamides with 3-(hydroxyimino)chromane-2,4-diones on silica gives 2,4-diaroyl-5-aminothiazoles, a class not made before, in 10 minutes at room temperature with no solvent and no metal catalyst. DFT and HRMS back a C(sp2)–S bond formation followed by dehydrative cyclization. Substrate scope reads broad for something done entirely by hand.

original_title: Investigation of α-Silylalcohols as Chiral Umpolung Carbanion Surrogates through Stereospecific 1,2-Brook Rearrangement
title: Racing a chiral carbanion before it forgets its own configuration
blurb: Chiral α-silyl secondary alcohols undergo a stereospecific 1,2-Brook rearrangement to spit out a polarity-reversed carbanion that, trapped fast enough, hasn't racemized yet. Using Weinreb amides as the electrophile gets enantioenriched α-hydroxyketones in good yield, but the ee swings with the substituents since it's really a race between trapping speed and racemization.

original_title: Unexpected effects of the addition of copper(II) bisphenanthroline complexes in Chan-Lam couplings
title: Adding copper phenanthroline to Chan-Lam couplings does something, just not the thing they were testing for
blurb: They added two copper(II) bisphenanthroline complexes to Chan-Lam couplings on the theory they'd act as redox shuttles. Neither one does, in either catalyst system. But dosing them into copper acetate-catalyzed reactions still juiced activity dramatically in some cases, for reasons that clearly aren't the mechanism they went looking for, while the LCuCl-catalyzed reactions just sat there unaffected.

original_title: Toward Rational Design of Orally Bioavailable PROTACs: Development of a Fully Computational Oral Absorption Score
title: A computational screen for whether your PROTAC survives being swallowed
blurb: PROTACs are big, polar, and floppy enough that oral absorption usually only gets sorted out after synthesis. comPASS is a fully computational scoring function built from molecular dynamics descriptors, weighing molecular extension against exposed polarity through a normalized radius of gyration, meant to flag likely absorption before you make the compound.

original_title: Histology-Guided Serial-Section Framework for Quasi-3D ToF-SIMS Molecular Imaging of Rat Brain Lipid Ions
title: Stitching flat ToF-SIMS lipid maps into a 3D rat brain
blurb: ToF-SIMS gives label-free lipid images but only one 2D slice at a time, missing anything that varies front-to-back. This workflow uses adjacent H&E-stained sections to align sparsely sampled ToF-SIMS slices into an anatomically referenced quasi-3D lipid map, then filters the resulting point clouds for whole-brain and region-specific views. Less a new measurement than a smarter way to stitch the ones you already have.

original_title: Long-Retention Fluorescent Probe for Plasma Membrane Imaging and Analysis of Membrane Remodeling
title: A membrane dye that actually stays in the membrane
blurb: Plasma membrane probes usually get internalized within hours, which muddies any real read on membrane remodeling. NIR-PMP-1 is a near-infrared molecular rotor that labels the membrane in 30 seconds, wash-free, and stays put with minimal internalization for up to 24 hours in both live and fixed cells. Enough runway to actually track membrane changes instead of chasing where the dye wandered off to.

original_title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Spiropyrrolidines by Synergistic Catalysis
title: Chiral acid and achiral palladium team up for spiropyrrolidines
blurb: Pairing a chiral phosphoric acid with an achiral palladium catalyst drives a formal [3+2] cycloaddition between activated vinylcyclopropanes and imidazolone-derived aldimines, building highly substituted spiropyrrolidines in one pot. Yields top out around 83% with dr up to 1:12, which is a decent return for a two-catalyst system where neither half alone would get you the stereocontrol.

original_title: Phosphate backbone epitranscriptomics: Discovery of natural RNA phosphorothioates and their writer machinery.
title: RNA turns out to carry its own phosphorothioate mark, and someone found the writer
blurb: Phosphorothioation was known as a DNA backbone modification. This paper finds it occurring naturally on RNA too, and identifies the machinery that installs it. A new class of backbone-level epitranscriptomic mark, not just another base tweak, which means the modified-RNA catalog has been missing a whole layer.

original_title: Formation of the titanium oxyl at an electrochemical interface: limiting the role of solvent re-orientation in strong electric fields
title: The titanium oxyl doesn't need the water to get out of the way much
blurb: Time-resolved mid-IR ATR catches the terminal oxygen intermediate forming at a titanium oxide electrode, and the energetics look more like vacuum-interface bond reorganization than a big free-energy assist from reorienting water dipoles and ions in the electrolyte. Useful if you've been modeling water oxidation catalysts with a heavy solvent-reorganization term baked in.

original_title: Chemoenzymatic synthesis of (E,E,Z)-humulene derived natural products
title: First synthesis of the humulene isomer nobody's touched
blurb: Most humulene meroterpenoid work runs through the well-studied (E,E,E) core. This is the first synthesis of (E,E,Z)-(10S)-hydroxyhumulene, carried through a chemoenzymatic route to the actual natural products, opening up a whole isomer's worth of bioactive macrocycles that had gone unexplored.

original_title: GaCl 3 -promoted C–H functionalization of ethylidenemalonate in reactions with internal alkynes
title: GaCl3 gets ethylidenemalonate doing C–H chemistry it hasn't done before
blurb: An unprecedented C(sp2)–H functionalization of ethylidenemalonate with internal alkynes, promoted by GaCl3, delivers substituted vinylcyclopentanes cleanly as the trans,trans isomer. New reactivity out of a pretty mundane building block.

original_title: A Modular Rapid-Injection NMR for Structure Elucidation and Kinetic Analysis
title: A rapid-injection NMR rig that doesn't need its own room
blurb: RI-NMR turns a standard NMR tube into a reaction vessel for watching intermediates form under real conditions, but bulky, facility-hogging instrument designs have kept it niche. This one's modular, built to bolt onto most existing spectrometers without taking over the magnet.

original_title: Modulation of structure, functionality, allergenicity and in vitro digestibility of ovalbumin through cold plasma-induced conjugation with rosemary-derived phenolic acids.
title: Cold plasma makes egg protein less allergenic, maybe
blurb: Zapping ovalbumin with cold plasma while conjugating it to rosemary-derived phenolic acids changes its structure and digestibility and dials down its allergenicity. Food chemistry rather than pharma, but the allergenicity angle is the one worth watching.

original_title: Phase I-II, FIH, TROP2 ADC, Advanced Unresectable/Metastatic Solid Tumors, Refractory to Standard Therapies (KL264-01)
title: Another TROP2 ADC lines up for the tumors that ran out of options
blurb: SKB264, Klus Pharma's TROP2-directed ADC, is in first-in-human Phase 1/2 for advanced or metastatic solid tumors refractory to standard therapy, with ovarian and gastric adenocarcinoma named specifically. It's active but not recruiting, so this is the trial running, not a readout.

original_title: Selectivity in Homolytic Substitution at a Tertiary Phosphine Center: Mechanistic Insights into Dealkanation Reaction
title: Making a phosphine spit out an alkane instead of doing the usual radical dance
blurb: Peri-substituted compounds with tertiary and secondary phosphine groups undergo dealkanation to give an alkane and a diphosphine, reversing the normal direction of radical P–C bond formation. Swapping alkyl groups on the tertiary phosphine and matching rates against computation pins the selectivity on how good a leaving group the departing radical is.

original_title: Dual-network hydrogel electrolytes based on carboxymethyl cellulose/tannic acid physical network and covalently crosslinked polyacrylic acid for flexible interdigital zinc-ion hybrid supercapacitors.
title: A cellulose-based hydrogel electrolyte for bendy zinc-ion supercapacitors
blurb: Dual-network design: a physical carboxymethyl cellulose/tannic acid network tangled with a covalently crosslinked polyacrylic acid one, built as the electrolyte for flexible interdigital zinc-ion hybrid supercapacitors. A materials design paper more than anything.

original_title: Second Harmonic Generation of Spiropyran–Merocyanine Photoswitches: Insights From Hyper‐Rayleigh Scattering and All‐Atom Dynamic Structure Quantum Mechanical Calculations
title: Watching spiropyran flip while measuring how hard it can shove light around
blurb: Hyper-Rayleigh scattering tracks second harmonic generation in two spiropyran/merocyanine photoswitches in dichloromethane while UV light drives the switching, paired with a new all-atom computational protocol, GFN2-xTB dynamics plus exact integral electrostatics, aimed at getting the nonlinear optical properties of the actual solvated system instead of a gas-phase stand-in.

original_title: Odd-Nuclearity in Homologous Series of Ni-Tiara Clusters Unlocking Near-Unity NH3 Selectivity in Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction
title: The odd one out in a nickel-cluster series turns out to be the ammonia specialist
blurb: A homologous series of atomically precise Ni-tiara clusters, Ni4, Ni5, and Ni6 with cyclopentylmethanethiolate ligands, gives a structurally defined platform for electrochemical nitrate reduction to ammonia, a reaction usually plagued by ambiguous active sites. The odd-nuclearity Ni5 cluster is the one that pushes selectivity to near-unity.

original_title: Mechanochemical Hydrazone Synthesis From Isoniazid and Isophthalaldehyde: Kinetics and Process Optimization of a Competitive‐Consecutive Reaction
title: Actually doing the kinetics on mechanochemical hydrazone synthesis
blurb: Ball-milling a hydrazone from isoniazid and isophthalaldehyde runs as a competitive-consecutive reaction, and instead of just quoting yield and reaction time like most mechanochemistry papers do, this one works out the actual kinetics and mixing-quality effects you'd need to scale the process up.

original_title: Visible-Light-Mediated C–N Cross-Coupling through Direct Sensitization of the Ni–BINAM Complex
title: The Ni-BINAM complex catalyzes its own photochemistry
blurb: A Ni-BINAM complex absorbs the visible light directly, so this C(sp2)-N coupling between aryl bromides and amines skips the external photocatalyst entirely. With aliphatic amines you don't even need the BINAM ligand, since the amine does double duty as coupling partner and ligand.

original_title: Quantitative Characterization of RNA-Splinted Ligation as a Multipurpose Post-Synthetic Strategy for High-Density DNA Microarrays Synthesized by Nucleic Acid Photolithography
title: Fixing photolithographic DNA microarrays after the fact with RNA-splinted ligation
blurb: Photolithography gives DNA microarrays full spatial control but racks up errors on long probes and can't touch photosensitive building blocks mid-synthesis. This quantifies RNA-splinted ligation as a post-synthetic patch, stitching pieces together afterward instead of fighting the photochemistry during synthesis.

original_title: Bicyclo[1.1.0]butane Carboxamides to N-Heterocycles via a Strain Release-Enabled Nickel(II)–Carbene Intermediate
title: Strained bicyclobutanes route to a nickel carbene, then to tetracyclic heterocycles
blurb: Strain release cracks open bicyclo[1.1.0]butane carboxamides into a new Ni(II)-carbene intermediate, caught with a trapping experiment, which then runs alkyne metathesis, cyclopropanation, and [4+2] cycloadditions to build cyclopropane-fused quinolinones and phenanthridinones. Broad scope and high yields, and they back it up with a synthetic application rather than just the methodology.

original_title: Fully Automated Purification of Small Molecules Using Online MicroSPE-UPLC-SPE
title: An automated purification line so NMR isn't the bottleneck
blurb: An online microSPE-UPLC setup takes up to 1 mL of extract, fractionates it across 96-well microSPE cartridges, and quantitatively transfers peaks to UPLC with a dual-pump loading scheme. Built to get unknown metabolite peaks purified for NMR without the usual slow manual cleanup.

original_title: Femtosecond Laser Writing of Stepwise Detachable and Biodegradable Microrobots for Adjustable Locomotion and Drug Delivery.
title: Microrobots that shed themselves in stages
blurb: Femtosecond laser writing builds biodegradable microrobots designed to detach piece by piece, giving them adjustable locomotion for drug delivery.

original_title: Stage-Defined Prenyltransferase Integration for Hybrid RiPP Biosynthesis
title: Timing matters when you bolt a foreign prenyltransferase onto a RiPP pathway
blurb: Hybrid RiPP biosynthesis means getting enzymes from unrelated pathway families to cooperate on the same peptide. Using in vitro biosynthesis to control exact timing, they added a cyanobactin prenyltransferase into thiopeptide assembly, and prenylating early or mid-pathway interfered with the other interdependent steps on that precursor peptide, so when you add it turns out to be the whole game.

original_title: Antimicrobial zwitterionic hydrogel coatings for kidney disease-associated catheters: current challenges and advances.
title: Rounding up zwitterionic hydrogel coatings for kidney catheters
blurb: A review of antimicrobial zwitterionic hydrogel coatings for catheters used in kidney disease, covering current challenges and where the field has moved. No new data, just a survey of the state of play.

original_title: Post-Fabrication Deprotection of Semiconducting Polymers for High-Performance Organic Electrochemical Transistors
title: Build the OECT first, deprotect the polymer after
blurb: OMIEC side-chain design for organic electrochemical transistors has always meant trading solubility for performance. This flips the order: coat with silyl-protected side chains that process just fine, then acid-cleave them post-fabrication to expose short alcohol-terminated chains that would've been too insoluble to coat in the first place.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Alpha Fusion Names Alison Armour CMO as At-211 Integration With Curadh Advances - citybiz
title: Alpha Fusion hires a CMO as its At-211 tie-up with Curadh moves along
blurb: Alpha Fusion has named Alison Armour chief medical officer while its At-211 integration with Curadh progresses. A leadership-hire announcement, light on any actual program detail.

original_title: Spatial proximity sequencing maps developmental dynamics in the germinal center
title: A new proximity assay that watches B cells pick a fate
blurb: Sprox-seq pairs proximity ligation with spatial transcriptomics, so it reads protein complexes, surface markers, and mRNA in the same intact tissue instead of guessing at colocalization from separate stains. Run on human tonsils, it maps the germinal center interaction network, ties CD21-CD35 complexes to proliferative programs, and catches B cells mid-transition between states, including direct contact with follicular dendritic cells. The interesting part is that it's reading interactions directly rather than inferring them from expression alone.
